facts.text: Hubbard County was officially organized on February 26, 1883, and named after Governor Lucius Frederick Hubbard, a Civil War veteran who championed railroad expansion.
The Hubbard County Historical Museum occupies a Victorian courthouse built in 1900, whose tin ceiling and green walls still echo its original design.
Before European arrival, Ojibwe bands used the county’s lakes, rivers, and pine forests for hunting, fishing, and wild rice gathering.
Routine spring floods along the Crow Wing River, such as those in 1965 and 1997, caused localized damage but were managed through diking and drainage improvements.
